title: Dose Titration Days in a Prescription Insurance on File Continuation Supply
content:
**Prescription Insurance on File** adds dose-overlap days to a continuation supply when the continued drug was recently refilled for a dosage change, as the fill ledger under Prescriptions shows. The continued drug is the prescription the most recent denial on the coverage concerns.

## Rule

- When a refill of the continued drug was dispensed for a **dosage change** less than **3** whole months before the date of service, **7** days are added for the dose overlap.
- When the most recent such refill of the continued drug was dispensed at least 3 but less than **6** whole months before, **3** days are added.
- Otherwise no titration days are added, and a dosage change of another prescription adds nothing.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, date of service 10 June)

| Most recent dosage-change refill of the continued drug | Whole months before 10 June | Days added |
|---|---|---|
| 11 March | 2 | 7 |
| 10 March | 3 | 3 |
| 11 December | 5 | 3 |
| 10 December | 6 | 0 |
| None | — | 0 |

## Points of judgement

- The refill must carry the fill reason "dosage change" in the Prescriptions fill ledger; a routine refill, a vacation refill or a lost-or-stolen replacement does not count.
- Only refills of the continued drug count: a dosage-change refill of another of the patient's prescriptions last month adds nothing.
